models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description:
Unauthenticated visitor tracking for browsing analytics and potential conversion to membership.

Guests represent anonymous users who browse the discussion board without creating an account. This table enables basic analytics on guest behavior, traffic patterns, and conversion funnels from guest to registered member. Each guest record is identified by a unique session identifier rather than personal information, maintaining privacy while enabling meaningful analytics.

Guests have read-only access to published articles and can view all public content. When a guest registers, they transition to member status and this guest record may be linked to track the conversion journey.

plainFields.name: session_identifier
plainFields.description: Unique session identifier for tracking guest browsing activity across visits. Generated on first visit and stored in browser.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the guest for basic analytics and abuse prevention. Used only for security monitoring and traffic analysis.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string for device and platform analytics. Helps understand guest device preferences.

plainFields.name: first_visit_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the guest's first visit to the platform. Used to calculate visitor recency and lifetime.

plainFields.name: last_visit_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the guest's most recent visit. Updated on each session to track engagement frequency.

plainFields.name: page_views
plainFields.description: Total number of page views by this guest across all visits. Indicates engagement level.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Registered members who create and participate in economic and political discussions.

Members are authenticated users who have completed registration and email verification. They can create articles, upload attachments, edit their own content, and engage with the discussion board beyond read-only access. Each member has a unique email address and username for authentication and public identification.

Members must verify their email address before gaining full content creation privileges. The verification status and password are managed to ensure security and account ownership. Members can update their profile information, change passwords, and manage their account lifecycle including voluntary account deletion.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all members and verified before full access.

plainFields.name: password
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Stored using bcrypt with work factor 10+. Never stored or transmitted in plain text.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique username for public identification in articles and profiles. Displayed as author name. Must be 3-30 characters.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Optional display name for public profile. If not set, username is used for display. Can be updated by member.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional member biography or description for public profile. Maximum 500 characters. Allows members to introduce themselves.

plainFields.name: avatar_url
plainFields.description: URL to profile avatar image. JPEG or PNG format, resized to 200x200 pixels. Optional member profile picture.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the member's email address has been verified. Must be true before allowing article creation and full member privileges.

plainFields.name: email_verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was completed. Null until member verifies their email address.

plainFields.name: is_suspended
plainFields.description: Whether the member account is currently suspended by moderators. Suspended members cannot login or create content.

plainFields.name: suspension_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for account suspension provided by moderator. Displayed to member on login attempt during suspension.

plainFields.name: suspended_until
plainFields.description: Timestamp when suspension expires and account is automatically reactivated. Null if not suspended or permanently banned.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of member's most recent successful login. Used for activity tracking and security monitoring.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created through registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was deleted. Supports soft deletion with 30-day retention before permanent removal.

models.name: discussion_board_moderators
models.description:
Trusted administrators with elevated privileges for content moderation and community management.

Moderators are authenticated users with special permissions to review, edit, and remove any content on the platform. They manage community guidelines enforcement, handle reported content, and can suspend or ban member accounts. Moderator privileges are granted by system administrators and cannot be self-assigned.

Moderators maintain transparency and accountability through comprehensive action logging. All moderation actions including content edits, deletions, and account suspensions are recorded with moderator identity and reasoning. Moderators have similar authentication requirements as members but with elevated access levels.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for moderator authentication and communication. Must be unique across all moderators and verified.

plainFields.name: password
plainFields.description: Hashed password for moderator authentication. Stored using bcrypt with work factor 10+. Never stored or transmitted in plain text.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique username for moderator identification in moderation logs and actions. Displayed when moderator edits content.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Optional display name for moderator profile. If not set, username is used for display.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the moderator's email address has been verified. Must be true before granting moderation privileges.

plainFields.name: email_verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when email verification was completed for this moderator account.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the moderator account is currently active. Inactive moderators cannot perform moderation actions or login.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of moderator's most recent successful login. Used for activity tracking and security monitoring.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created by system administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderator privileges were revoked and account deleted. Supports soft deletion for audit trail.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Active authentication sessions for registered members enabling secure stateless authentication.

Each session represents a member's authenticated connection to the platform. Sessions are created upon successful login and used to validate member identity for subsequent requests. Session management uses JWT tokens with 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration.

Sessions track connection context including IP address and referrer for security monitoring and abuse detection. Multiple concurrent sessions are supported allowing members to access the platform from different devices. Sessions are invalidated on logout or token expiration.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who owns this authentication session. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the member's connection for this session. Used for security monitoring and geographic analysis.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the session was initiated. Typically the login page or authentication endpoint.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating how the member arrived at the login page. Used for traffic source analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created through successful member login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was terminated. Null for active sessions, set on logout or token expiration.

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Active authentication sessions for moderators enabling secure access to moderation tools.

Each session represents a moderator's authenticated connection to the platform. Sessions are created upon successful moderator login and used to validate moderator identity and privileges for moderation operations. Session management uses JWT tokens with 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration.

Moderator sessions track connection context for security auditing and accountability. All moderation actions performed during a session can be traced back to the specific moderator and session for comprehensive audit trails.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who owns this authentication session. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the moderator's connection for this session. Used for security monitoring and access control.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL where the moderator session was initiated. Typically the moderator login page.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating how the moderator arrived at the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderator session was created through successful login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was terminated. Null for active sessions, set on logout or token expiration.

models.name: discussion_board_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for confirming member email address ownership during registration.

Email verification is required before members can create articles and access full platform features. Upon registration, a verification token is generated and sent to the member's email address. The member must click the verification link within 24 hours to activate their account.

Each verification record contains a unique token with expiration timestamp. Tokens are single-use and invalidated after successful verification or expiration. Members can request new verification emails if the original token expires.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account requiring email verification. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to member's email address. Generated using cryptographically secure random string.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address being verified. Stored to ensure verification links work even if member changes their email.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token expires. Tokens are valid for 24 hours from creation.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member successfully verified their email using this token. Null if not yet verified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was generated and sent to the member.

models.name: discussion_board_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset requests for secure password recovery supporting both members and moderators.

This main entity stores the core password reset data including the unique token, target email address, and expiration timestamp. The actor_type field discriminates between member and moderator reset requests, enabling polymorphic ownership while maintaining proper normalization.

Each reset request generates a cryptographically secure token sent to the user's registered email address. Tokens expire after 1 hour for security. The token allows users to set a new password without knowing their current password. Reset tokens are single-use and invalidated after successful password change.

The actual relationship to the specific member or moderator is maintained through separate subtype tables (discussion_board_password_reset_of_members and discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators), following the Compatible Actor Pattern for proper 3NF normalization.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor requesting password reset. Valid values: 'member' or 'moderator'. Discriminator field for polymorphic ownership pattern.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token sent to user's email address. Generated using cryptographically secure random string for security.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address where the reset link was sent. Stored to validate reset requests against current account email.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token expires. Tokens are valid for 1 hour from creation for security.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token was successfully used to change password. Null if not yet used.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset request was created and token was sent.

models.name: discussion_board_password_reset_of_members
models.description:
Member-specific password reset context linking reset requests to member accounts.

This subtype entity maintains the 1:1 relationship between password reset requests and specific member accounts. It enables proper normalization of the polymorphic ownership pattern where password resets can be initiated by either members or moderators.

Each record associates a password reset token with the member who requested it, enabling the system to validate reset requests and apply password changes to the correct account. The unique constraint on discussion_board_password_reset_id ensures each reset request is associated with exactly one member.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_password_reset_id
foreignFields.description: Password reset request associated with this member. {@link discussion_board_password_resets.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this member password reset association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators
models.description:
Moderator-specific password reset context linking reset requests to moderator accounts.

This subtype entity maintains the 1:1 relationship between password reset requests and specific moderator accounts. It enables proper normalization of the polymorphic ownership pattern where password resets can be initiated by either members or moderators.

Each record associates a password reset token with the moderator who requested it, enabling the system to validate reset requests and apply password changes to the correct account. The unique constraint on discussion_board_password_reset_id ensures each reset request is associated with exactly one moderator.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_password_reset_id
foreignFields.description: Password reset request associated with this moderator. {@link discussion_board_password_resets.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator account requesting password reset. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderator password reset association was created.

models.name: discussion_board_article_categories
models.description:
Predefined discussion categories for organizing articles by topic area.

Stores the available category options (Economic Discussion, Political Discussion, General Discussion) that members select when creating articles. Categories help users discover relevant discussions and browse articles by topic focus.

Each category has a unique name and optional description explaining the types of discussions that belong to it. Categories are managed by administrators and provide the organizational taxonomy for the entire discussion board.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category display name shown to users. Examples: 'Economic Discussion', 'Political Discussion', 'General Discussion'. Must be unique across all categories.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-friendly category identifier derived from name. Used in category filter URLs and routing. Must be unique and lowercase with hyphens.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional explanation of what types of articles belong in this category. Helps members choose the appropriate category when creating articles. Can include topic guidelines and examples.

plainFields.name: sort_order
plainFields.description: Display order for category lists. Lower numbers appear first. Allows administrators to prioritize category presentation in UI.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was created by administrators. Used for category management and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when category details (name, description, sort order) were last modified. Updated whenever administrators edit category information.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Discussion articles created by members on economic and political topics.

Represents the core content of the discussion board where members share their perspectives, analyses, and discussions. Each article has a title, rich text body content, belongs to exactly one category, and is authored by a registered member.

Articles progress through lifecycle states: draft (work in progress), published (publicly visible), and archived (hidden but preserved). The deleted_at timestamp enables soft deletion for content that is removed but may need recovery.

Members can create unlimited articles, edit their own articles at any time, and delete their own content. Moderators have elevated permissions to edit any article for quality control or delete articles that violate community guidelines.

Articles support rich text formatting, can include image and file attachments (stored in separate attachment tables), and track engagement through view counts. Edit history is preserved through updated_at timestamps and is_edited flags for transparency.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category this article belongs to. References discussion_board_article_categories {@link discussion_board_article_categories.id}. Required for article organization and discovery.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who authored this article. References discussion_board_members {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Establishes article ownership and attribution.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title summarizing the discussion topic. Must be between 5 and 200 characters. Displayed in article lists and detail pages for content discovery.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-friendly identifier derived from title. Used in article URLs for readability and SEO. Must be unique across all articles to ensure distinct URLs.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main article content with rich text formatting. Contains the full discussion text including paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, lists, and blockquotes. Minimum 50 characters, maximum 50,000 characters to ensure substantive content.

plainFields.name: excerpt
plainFields.description: Brief preview text extracted from the first 200 characters of body content. Used in article listings to help users identify relevant discussions without reading full content.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Publication state of the article. Valid values: 'draft' (work in progress, visible only to author), 'published' (publicly visible to all users), 'archived' (hidden from public view but preserved). Controls article visibility and lifecycle.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this article has been viewed by any user. Incremented each time a user accesses the article detail page. Used to identify popular content and measure engagement.

plainFields.name: is_edited
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this article has been edited after initial publication. Set to true when a published article is modified. Provides transparency about content revisions to readers.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this article was first published (transitioned from draft to published state). Null for articles that have never been published. Used for chronological sorting and publication date display.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this article was initially created, regardless of publication state. Used for tracking content creation patterns and article age.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article content (title, body, category) was last modified. Updated on every edit. Displayed to readers to indicate content freshness and recent revisions.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp indicating when this article was deleted by author or moderator. Null for active articles. Enables 30-day retention period for potential recovery before permanent deletion.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
Image and file attachments supporting discussion articles with visual evidence, charts, documents, and reference materials.

Each attachment belongs to exactly one article and is uploaded by a specific member during article creation or editing. The unified table handles both image attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP up to 5MB, maximum 10 per article) and document attachments (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV up to 10MB, maximum 5 per article).

Attachments are managed exclusively through their parent articles. When articles are deleted, all associated attachments are removed. The type field discriminates between image and file attachments, while format specifies the exact file format. Size and original filename are preserved for display and download purposes.

Storage paths reference the physical file location in the storage system. Attachments undergo security validation including file type verification, size limit enforcement, and malware scanning during upload. Soft deletion is supported to maintain attachment lifecycle management and enable recovery if needed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who uploaded this attachment. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Attachment type discriminator. Valid values: 'image' for visual content (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), 'file' for documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV). Determines size limits and display handling.

plainFields.name: format
plainFields.description: File format extension indicating the specific attachment format. Examples: 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'pdf', 'doc', 'docx', 'xls', 'xlsx', 'txt', 'csv'. Used for validation and download MIME type determination.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Used to enforce size limits (images: 5MB max, documents: 10MB max) and display file size to users in human-readable format.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename provided by user during upload. Preserved for display purposes and download filename. Maximum 255 characters.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: Internal storage path or reference to the physical file location in the storage system. Used by application to retrieve and serve the file. Not exposed to end users.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded and created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the attachment record. Updated when attachment metadata changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates the attachment has been removed and should not be displayed. Null for active attachments. Enables recovery and maintains referential integrity during deletion workflows.

models.name: discussion_board_content_reports
models.description:
Member-submitted reports flagging articles for policy violations or inappropriate content.

Stores community-driven content moderation reports where members flag articles that may violate community guidelines, contain spam, misinformation, offensive content, or other policy violations. Each report captures the reporting member's concerns, selected violation category, and optional detailed explanation.

Reports are added to the moderation queue for moderator review. Multiple members can report the same article independently, with each report tracked separately. Moderators review reports and take appropriate action (approve content, edit content, or remove content), then mark reports as resolved.

The reporting system enables collaborative content quality management by empowering the community to identify problematic content while maintaining moderator oversight and final decision authority.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reported article that allegedly violates community guidelines. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who submitted this content report. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: resolved_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who reviewed and resolved this report. Null if report is still pending review. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: report_category
plainFields.description: Category of policy violation being reported. Valid values include 'Spam', 'Offensive Content', 'Misinformation', 'Off-Topic', 'Other'. Helps moderators prioritize and categorize reports.

plainFields.name: report_details
plainFields.description: Optional detailed explanation from the reporter describing the specific policy violation or concern. Provides context to help moderators understand the issue.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current resolution status of the report. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting moderator review), 'reviewed_no_action' (moderator found no violation), 'reviewed_edited' (moderator edited content), 'reviewed_removed' (moderator removed content). Tracks report lifecycle.

plainFields.name: resolution_notes
plainFields.description: Moderator's notes explaining the resolution decision. Provides transparency about why the report was handled in a specific way. Null if report is still pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was submitted by the member. Used for prioritizing older reports and tracking moderation response time.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was reviewed and resolved by a moderator. Null if report is still pending. Used for measuring moderation response time.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail of all moderator actions for accountability and transparency.

Records every content moderation and user management action taken by moderators, including article edits, article deletions, attachment removals, account suspensions, and account bans. Each log entry captures what action was taken, which moderator performed it, what content or user was affected, when it occurred, and the moderator's documented reason.

The moderation log serves multiple critical purposes: accountability (tracking who did what and why), transparency (allowing review of moderation decisions), dispute resolution (providing evidence for appeals), and pattern analysis (identifying problematic content or users requiring escalated action).

Log entries are immutable and retained indefinitely per business requirements. Moderators and administrators can search and filter logs by action type, moderator, affected content, affected user, or time period to review moderation history, investigate specific incidents, or generate moderation activity reports.

This comprehensive audit trail ensures moderation decisions are documented, reviewable, and consistent with community guidelines.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who performed this moderation action. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article that was moderated (edited, deleted, or had attachments removed). Null if action was user account management rather than content moderation. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member whose account was affected by moderator action (suspension, ban, or account restoration). Null if action was content moderation rather than account management. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: 'article_edited' (moderator edited article content), 'article_deleted' (moderator removed article), 'attachment_removed' (moderator deleted specific attachment), 'account_suspended' (member account temporarily suspended), 'account_banned' (member account permanently banned), 'account_restored' (suspension or ban reversed). Categorizes the moderation action.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Moderator's documented explanation for taking this action. Required for all moderation actions to ensure accountability and transparency. Examples: 'Removed spam content', 'Suspended for harassment', 'Edited to remove personal information'.

plainFields.name: action_details
plainFields.description: Additional contextual details about the moderation action. May include what was changed in an edit, which attachment was removed, or specific policy violations. Provides complete context for audit trail.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed. Used for chronological audit trail, moderation activity reporting, and tracking response times.

models.name: discussion_board_account_actions
models.description:
Record of account-level moderation actions including suspensions and bans.

Tracks all temporary suspensions and permanent bans applied to member accounts, maintaining a complete history of disciplinary actions. Each record captures which member was affected, which moderator applied the action, the reason for the action, the duration (for suspensions), and the current status (active, expired, or reversed).

Temporary suspensions prevent members from logging in and creating content for a specified duration (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). When the suspension period expires, the account is automatically restored to active status. Permanent bans prevent all future access and are typically reserved for severe or repeated policy violations.

Moderators can reverse suspensions or bans if they were applied in error. All status changes are tracked with timestamps to maintain a complete audit trail. The action history helps moderators make informed decisions about escalating enforcement (warnings → short suspension → long suspension → permanent ban) based on violation patterns.

This table enables moderators to search and filter account actions by affected member, moderating moderator, action type, or time period to review enforcement history and ensure consistent application of community guidelines.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member whose account was suspended or banned. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who applied this account suspension or ban. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

foreignFields.name: reversed_by_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who reversed or lifted this suspension or ban. Null if action has not been reversed. {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of account action applied. Valid values: 'suspension' (temporary account block), 'ban' (permanent account block). Determines whether the action has an expiration date.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Moderator's documented reason for suspending or banning the account. Required for accountability and to inform the affected member. Examples: 'Repeated spam violations', 'Harassment of other members', 'Severe policy violation'.

plainFields.name: duration_days
plainFields.description: Duration of suspension in days (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). Null for permanent bans which have no expiration. Used to calculate expiration timestamp for temporary suspensions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the account action. Valid values: 'active' (currently in effect), 'expired' (suspension period ended), 'reversed' (moderator lifted the action). Determines whether the member is currently blocked.

plainFields.name: reversal_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation for why the suspension or ban was reversed by a moderator. Null if action has not been reversed. Examples: 'Applied in error', 'User successfully appealed', 'Circumstances changed'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the suspension or ban was applied. Used to calculate expiration time for temporary suspensions and to track enforcement history chronologically.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a temporary suspension will automatically expire and the account will be restored. Null for permanent bans. System automatically updates status to 'expired' when this time is reached.

plainFields.name: reversed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a moderator reversed or lifted the suspension or ban. Null if action has not been reversed. Tracks when account access was manually restored.
